Definition: from G5279; a reminding or (reflexively) recollection:--remembrance.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, hypómnēsis is the word for remembrance. In 2 Timothy 1:5, the text says "When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee." In 2 Peter 1:13, the text says "to stir you up by putting [you] in remembrance."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: hypómnēsis tells me that remembering is how faith stays alive — we look back at what God did so we trust Him for what comes next. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
